extracted.subtask_description: Creating and evaluating printed type specimens to choose typeface, point size, leading, style, and face variations for book or printed matter. The page shows multiple typefaces, point sizes, leading options, and specimen texts to inspect appearance in use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens are shown at many point sizes (e.g., 'SIX POINT', 'SEVEN POINT', 'EIGHT POINT', 'NINE POINT', 'TEN POINT', 'ELEVEN POINT', 'TWELVE POINT', 'FOURTEEN POINT').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these labeled specimens to judge legibility, weight, and color of the face at each body size; compare the same paragraph at different sizes to assess suitability for body text, captions, or display use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface / face name
rubrics_metrics.description: Named faces and systems are displayed: 'MONOTYPE', 'CASLON OLD STYLE', 'SCOTCH ROMAN', plus numbered faces like 'NO. EIGHT', 'NO. TWENTY-FIVE', 'NO. THIRTY-SIX'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate face by comparing the same text set in each named type to observe character shapes, overall color, and tonal differences between designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaded vs Solid (leading specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens are explicitly labeled '[Leaded]' or '[Solid]' next to point-size/face headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaded indicates added line spacing; solid indicates minimal/no added leading. Compare leaded vs solid samples to choose line spacing that optimizes readability and page color for the chosen point size and face.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style (Roman vs Italic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Italic specimens are shown (e.g., 'EIGHT POINT ITALIC NO. TWENTY-FIVE K') alongside Roman/regular samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate italic cuts for slant, contrast, and harmony with the roman; use specimens to check emphasis, readability of italic text at body sizes, and consistency with the regular face.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point face / face casting note
rubrics_metrics.description: Some specimens indicate face casting details (e.g., 'TWELVE POINT GUSHING NO. TWENTY-FIVE (11 PT. FACE)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notes show that a face may be cast on a different body (an 11 pt face used for 12 pt setting). Use this information to understand optical and mechanical differences caused by face/ body mismatches when choosing type for production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen text in use (paragraph sample)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long paragraph samples ('When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius saw the fall of Carthage and of Corinth...') are set repeatedly to show 'SPECIMENS OF TYPES IN USE.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph samples demonstrate real-world appearance (measure, word spacing, color, rivers, hyphenation behavior). Use them to evaluate readability, text color, and overall suitability of a face for continuous reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-set and element samples (letters, ligatures, figures, punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short runs and miscellaneous specimens show characters and combinations: vowel runs 'aeiou', repeated letters 'aaaaaa eeeeee ill oooooo', numerals '1234567890', ligatures and special characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect these samples to assess individual glyph design, spacing, kerning, figure style (lining vs oldstyle), quality of diacritics/ligatures, and behavior of common letter combinations at different sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uppercase/display appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: All-caps and display lines are provided (e.g., lines set in capitals such as 'WHEN THOUGHTFUL GREEKS LIKE POLYBIUS SAW...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the uppercase/display specimens to judge headline presence, tracking/word-spacing in capitals, and suitability of the face for emphasis or display settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundry / casting system indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: System or casting method headers appear (for example, 'MONOTYPE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The casting/system label indicates production method and may affect availability, possible widths, and mechanical characteristics; consider system compatibility when specifying type for production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series/numbering identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Faces are identified with series numbers (e.g., 'NO. EIGHT', 'NO. TWENTY-FIVE', 'NO. THIRTY-SIX'), sometimes combined with family names ('CASLON OLD STYLE', 'SCOTCH ROMAN').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series numbers denote specific cuts/variations; record the exact series when ordering or matching types to ensure consistent reproduction.
